question.name: Questions: a rising voice or a question word
question.about: A yes/no question keeps the order of a statement, with the voice rising on the word asked about (Ты говоришь по-английски?), a question word like как, где or что often comes first, and Russian adds no do.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

question.short: A yes/no question keeps a statement's order, the voice rising: Машина здесь? (car here?). A question word most often comes first: Где машина?

no-be.name: No am, is or are in the present
no-be.about: Russian leaves out am, is and are in the present: Я студент (I'm a student); Где мои ключи? (Where are my keys?).

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

no-be.short: Russian leaves out am, is and are in the present: Я дома (I at home: I'm at home), Где ключ? (where key?).

have.name: Having: у меня есть
have.about: To say you have something, Russian says it is at you: У меня есть брат (I have a brother); when what matters is what it's like, not whether it's there, есть is often left out: У меня большая комната.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

have.short: To have is to be at you: У меня есть работа (at me is work: I have work); with none, нет and the genitive: У меня нет работы.

present.name: Present tense endings
present.about: The verb changes for each person: я живу, ты живёшь, он живёт, мы живём, они живут.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

present.short: The verb's ending says who: я пью, ты пьёшь, он пьёт (I drink, you drink, he drinks).

infinitive.name: When the next verb is an infinitive
infinitive.about: After words like можешь, хочу, люблю, дай and пора, the next verb stays in its dictionary form: можешь закрыть, хочу съесть, дай знать, пора идти.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

infinitive.short: After хочу, могу and the like, the next verb stays in its dictionary form: Я хочу пить (I want drink), Я могу помочь.

plural.name: Plurals
plural.about: In their basic (nominative) form, plural nouns mostly end in -ы or -и, or -а or -я (ключи, дела); adjectives and possessives such as мой take plural forms too (новые, мои), and some meanings are normally plural (выходные, the weekend).

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

plural.short: Most plurals end in -ы or -и, some in -а or -я: ключи, машины, дела.

gender.name: Masculine, feminine, neuter
gender.about: Most nouns ending in a consonant are masculine, most in -а or -я feminine and most in -о or -е neuter (though words for men stay masculine: папа), and adjectives, possessives such as мой and a singular past-tense verb agree with them.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

gender.short: Most nouns are он words, она words or оно words, and words with them match: мой телефон, моя сумка, моё молоко.

adjective.name: Adjectives match
adjective.about: An adjective matches its noun's gender, number and case: новый дом, новая куртка, новые ботинки, в маленькой квартире.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

adjective.short: An adjective matches its noun's gender, number and case: новый дом, новая машина, в новой машине.

accusative.name: The accusative: objects, where you go, when
accusative.about: A direct object often takes the accusative (Мы ели пиццу); so does where you're going after в or на (в магазин, на работу), and many expressions of time (в субботу).

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

accusative.short: What you drink, read or see takes the accusative; for -а words it ends in -у: Я пью воду, Я читаю книгу.

genitive.name: Of, without: the genitive
genitive.about: The genitive can mean of (машина папы, чашка чая), follows без, из and у, and comes after many amounts and numbers: без сахара, десять минут.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

genitive.short: The genitive says of, and follows для, без, из and у: машина мамы (car of Mom), для мамы, у меня.

genitive-negation.name: нет + genitive
genitive-negation.about: To say there isn't something, use нет and the genitive: нет молока, У меня нет времени; and не будет for the future.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

genitive-negation.short: With нет, what isn't there takes the genitive: У меня нет работы (at me no work), нет молока.

prepositional.name: Where and how: в or на + prepositional
prepositional.about: With в or на, where something is takes the prepositional, usually ending in -е: в Москве, на столе, в холодильнике; and how you travel: на автобусе.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

prepositional.short: After в and на, where something is mostly ends in -е: на столе, в сумке, в машине.

dative.name: To someone: the dative
dative.about: The dative is to or for someone: Я позвоню тебе; and the one who feels or likes: Мне холодно (I'm cold), Мне нравится (I like it).

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

dative.short: The dative says to or for someone, and who feels something: Я дам тебе (I'll give you), Мне холодно (to me cold: I'm cold).

instrumental.name: With, as, and за
instrumental.about: The instrumental follows с (with: с мамой), says what you work as (Я работаю врачом), and follows за for going to get something (за хлебом).

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

instrumental.short: After с (with), a word takes the instrumental: кофе с молоком (coffee with milk), со мной (with me).

direction.name: Where you are, where you go
direction.about: Going and being somewhere differ: куда and где, домой and дома, сюда and здесь; в магазин (to the store) but в магазине (in the store).

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

direction.short: Being somewhere and going there are different words: дома (at home), домой (home, going there); здесь and сюда.

ne.name: не before what it denies
ne.about: не (not) goes right before the word it denies, and stays even with никогда (never): Я не знаю; Я никогда не был.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

ne.short: не goes right before what it denies: Я не пью кофе (I not drink coffee). There's no do.

past.name: Past tense by gender
past.about: The past says the gender in the singular, not the person (он был, она была, они были; a woman says я купила, a man я купил), and some pasts describe how things are now: ты устал (you're tired).

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

past.short: The past says the gender, not the person: он был, она была, они были; a woman says я была.

future.name: Talking about the future
future.about: Use буду and an imperfective infinitive for an action seen as ongoing, repeated or not about finishing it (never буду купить); the present for a plan (Завтра я еду на работу); будет for what there will be (Завтра будет дождь); a present-looking perfective for one whole action (Я позвоню); and the future after если too (Если не будет дождя, мы пойдём на пляж).

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

future.short: буду with an infinitive for what will be going on (Я буду читать); a perfective verb's present form for what will get done (Я прочитаю).

aspect.name: Two verbs for one action
aspect.about: Many verbs come in pairs: one for an action going on or repeated (покупать, звонить), one for the action as one finished whole (купить, позвонить).

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

aspect.short: Most verbs come in pairs: one for going on or again (читать), one for done once (прочитать).

motion.name: Going: идти or ехать
motion.about: For one trip, going now or planned, идти is going on foot (and coming or leaving: Иди сюда; Мне пора идти) and ехать going by car, bus or train; ходить and ездить are for regular trips, or there and back; пойти and поехать set off on one trip.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

motion.short: идти is going on foot, ехать going in something; for one trip now or planned: Я иду домой, Я еду домой.

new-last.name: What's new goes last
new-last.about: Russian order is free-ish, and the new information often comes late, so the subject can follow the verb: На столе лежит книга (on the table lies a book).

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

new-last.short: What's new often comes last, so the subject can follow the verb: На столе лежит ключ (on the table lies a key).

address.name: Informal ты, polite вы
address.about: ты and its verb forms speak to one person you know well, and вы and its forms to several people or politely to one, such as a waiter, a stranger or an older adult (Принесите, пожалуйста; Извините), so use вы with an adult you don't know until they offer ты.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

address.short: ты is for one person you know well, вы for someone you don't or for more than one, with the plural verb: Вы идёте домой?

imperative.name: Telling someone to do something
imperative.about: The command form has its own ending and no subject: Закрой дверь! Иди сюда! Дай мне знать! (-те for more people or politely: Принесите.)

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

imperative.short: The command form has no subject: Иди домой! Дай мне ключ! For вы, -те: Идите домой!

possessive.name: My, your: мой, твой
possessive.about: мой (my) and твой (your) match their noun like an adjective: мой ключ, моя сумка, моё молоко, мои ключи. его (his), её (her) and их (their) never change: его машина, её телефон.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Added in revision 2 for lessons 1–20.

possessive.short: мой and твой match their noun: мой ключ, моя сумка, моё молоко; его, её and их never change.

demonstrative.name: This: этот, это
demonstrative.about: этот (this) matches its noun: этот телефон, эта сумка, это молоко. это on its own says this is or it's, with no is: Это мой ключ (this my key: this is my key).

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Added in revision 2 for lessons 1–20.

demonstrative.short: этот matches its noun (этот телефон, эта сумка); это alone says this is: Это мой ключ (this my key).

short-adjective.name: Ready, glad: short adjectives
short-adjective.about: A few adjectives have a short form for how someone is, and like the past it says the gender: Я готов (I'm ready, a man says), Я готова (a woman says), Мы готовы (we're ready).

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Added in revision 2 for lessons 1–20.

short-adjective.short: A few adjectives have a short form for how someone is, and it says the gender: Я готов (a man), Я готова (a woman), Мы готовы.
